audit.whatIsWrong: Maokai is called 'the rare immobile melee' in early and 'an immobile, dash-less Maokai' in whys[4] and wants.you[0]. He has a dash, and it is the ability the rest of the entry is built around.
audit.why: Riot's text for Twisted Advance: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target.' It is 14/13/12/11/10 at 525 range. Calling him immobile while also telling the player to bait his dash is a contradiction the player has to resolve mid-lane.
audit.corrected: Rewrote early, wants.you[0] and whys[4] around the real ability, and the level-6 plan now waits for it rather than assuming it is absent.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Twisted Advance comes back up faster than your full Q-W-E combo cycle' is asserted with no numbers on either side, and it is the stated reason Levels 4-5 are lost.
audit.why: Twisted Advance is 14/13/12/11/10. Ambessa's Lacerate is 13/12/11/10/9 and Repudiation 18/17/16/15/14. At rank 1 his root is 14s against her 13s and 18s — the claim is true, but only because Repudiation is the long pole. Bramble Smash at 7/6.5/6/5.5/5 is the cooldown that actually breaks up her chain, and Sapling Toss is 18/17/16/15/14.
audit.corrected: Real numbers in mid, whys[3], breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Twisted Advance's untargetability is never mentioned, and it is the one interaction that can waste a 130-second ultimate.
audit.why: Riot's text: he becomes 'untargetable and dashing to the target'. Public Execution picks 'the farthest enemy champion in a line' — an untargetable Maokai is not a champion it can pick. Firing R at a Maokai already in transit either whiffs or blinks you to somebody else entirely. The correct sequencing is: let the root land, then R.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text, spikes[2].text, mid and whys[4] all now say fire R after the dash, never into it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sap Magic is named but its actual rule is never given, so the entry says 'he sustains through your chip' without saying why chipping is the problem.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Maokai's basic attack also heals him and deals additional damage on a moderate cooldown. Each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy's spell, this cooldown is reduced.' Every ability you land on him brings his next heal forward. Poking a Maokai is not neutral — it accelerates the thing beating you, which is why Grievous Wounds and not more chip is the answer.
audit.corrected: Stated in spikes[0].text, early, whys[0], late and phases[1].why, with the anti-heal call in spikes[3].text and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: 'R's armor-pen passive and ability-damage healing' is given as the reason the level-6 all-in works, in spikes[1], wants.you[2] and mid. Neither exists.
audit.why: Riot's Public Execution text: she 'blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line of her choosing and suppresses them upon her arrival. She then slams the enemy into the ground where they take damage and are stunned.' No penetration, no healing, no passive. The kit file's derived 'heal' flag on her R contradicts the description it was derived from.
audit.corrected: Replaced everywhere with the real mechanics — 1250-range blink, suppression on arrival, the slam stun — and an honest Grievous Wounds call where the fake healing used to be.

audit.whatIsWrong: early tells the player to 'farm with the outer edge of your cone where it deals double damage'.
audit.why: Riot's Cunning Sweep text says she 'sweeps her twin drakehounds in a semicircle in front of her, dealing bonus damage to enemies hit by the blades'. The bonus is for being hit by the blades, not for standing at the outer edge, and no multiplier is given anywhere. 'Double damage' is a number the data does not contain.
audit.corrected: early now says to farm with the blades of the cone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nature's Grasp is never named in either layer, so the late-game section says 'his ult zone or lock your carries' without telling the player what to dodge.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Maokai summons a colossal wall of brambles and thorns that slowly advances forwards, damaging and rooting any enemies in the path.' It is 3000 range on 130/110/90 and it travels — sidestepping is a lateral move, not a backwards one, and Drakehound's Step is exactly the tool for it.
audit.corrected: Named in late with its range.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Ambessa four of seven stages and Maokai none, while the whys text on five of those stages says Maokai is winning, and the recorded win rate is 47.57% against Ambessa.
audit.why: Chart and prose disagree with each other and with the data. I did not change any side or rating — a one-word side flip falls outside the length band the applier enforces, and there is no maokai/ambessa mirror yet to reconcile against. Raised as a question instead.
audit.corrected: Left win[] and phases[].side untouched. whys[6] left unedited rather than rewritten into a claim that Ambessa wins two-plus items, which the kits do not support.

edits.before: Maokai's passive (Sap Magic) and Sapling Toss let him heal back every Cunning Sweep cone you chip in, so he sits even-to-ahead while your Q/E cooldowns are still long.
edits.after: Sap Magic heals him on attack, and every spell you land on him shortens that cooldown — chipping a Cunning Sweep cone in pays for his sustain while your Q and E sit long.

edits.before: Public Execution blinks you behind an immobile Maokai, suppresses then stuns him, and the armor-pen passive + ability-damage healing make it your one clean all-in before he stacks armor.
edits.after: Public Execution blinks 1250 to the farthest champion in the line and suppresses on arrival — but it cannot pick him while Twisted Advance has him untargetable, so fire it after the root lands.

edits.before: Twisted Advance is the trade-ender: he dashes to you and roots you in place, cutting your Drakehound's Step dash-weave dead — never commit a Q-into-empowered-auto chain with his W up.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is the trade-ender: he goes untargetable, dashes onto you and roots — 14s at rank 1, and nothing you cast touches him in transit. Never commit a chain with his W up.

edits.before: Even on your Eclipse/Profane Hydra spike, his Bramble Vest/armor stacking plus passive sustain mean your physical-only burst chunks then heals off — you cannot delete a tank like a squishy.
edits.after: Even on your Eclipse/Profane Hydra spike, armour plus Sap Magic mean your physical-only burst chunks then heals off — buy Grievous Wounds or you cannot delete a tank like a squishy.

edits.before: Hit Level 6 and Public Execution him off his sapling line — suppress an immobile target with no dash to escape it
edits.after: Hit Level 6 and Public Execution him off his sapling line — suppress him the moment Twisted Advance is spent

edits.before: Bait Twisted Advance, then Q-into-empowered-auto weave with your Drakehound's Step dash only after his root whiffs
edits.after: Bait Twisted Advance's 14s, then Q-into-empowered-auto weave with Drakehound's Step once the root has whiffed

edits.before: Lean on R's armor-pen passive and ability-damage healing to win the short burst window before his sustain refills
edits.after: Buy Grievous Wounds early and win the short burst window before Sap Magic refills what your combo took off

edits.before: Land Twisted Advance to root your dash chain and end every trade on his terms
edits.after: Go untargetable through Twisted Advance, then root your dash chain dead

edits.before: Toss saplings and ride Sap Magic sustain to heal off your Cunning Sweep chip at no cost
edits.after: Toss saplings and let every spell you land on him shorten Sap Magic's heal timer

edits.before: Maokai is the rare immobile melee you do NOT free-trade into early, because his Sap Magic passive and Sapling Toss heal back every Cunning Sweep cone you land while your Q and E are still on long cooldowns. Don't walk up to throw the first Q into Bramble Smash range — his Twisted Advance dashes onto you and roots you the instant you commit, and his Q knockback shoves you off your Sundering Slam follow-up. Farm with the outer edge of your cone where it deals double damage, respect his sapling zoning around the bush, and accept that you concede this opening.
edits.after: Maokai is the rare melee you do NOT free-trade into early: Sap Magic heals him on attack and every spell you land on him shortens that heal's cooldown, so chipping a Cunning Sweep cone in actually pays for his sustain. Don't walk up into Bramble Smash's 600 range — its knockback shoves you off your Sundering Slam follow-up, and Twisted Advance goes untargetable, dashes onto you and roots the instant you commit. Farm with the blades of your cone, respect saplings in the bush, and accept that you concede this opening.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still his — Twisted Advance comes back up faster than your full Q-W-E combo cycle and he simply sustains through your chip. Level 6 is your one real flip: Public Execution blinks you behind him, suppresses and stuns a target with no dash to answer it, and the R passive's armor pen plus ability-damage healing let you actually commit a full combo. Save R to punish him stepping up to last-hit or to catch him off a sapling line — but if his W is up, bait the root first or he dashes in and cancels your all-in.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still his — Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 against your 13s Lacerate and 18s Repudiation, and he sustains through the chip. Level 6 is your one real flip: Public Execution blinks 1250 to the farthest champion in the line, suppresses and stuns, and a suppressed Maokai cannot cast anything. But it cannot pick him at all while Twisted Advance has him untargetable — bait the root out, then fire R after the dash, never into it. Save it for him stepping up to last-hit or for catching him off a sapling line.

edits.before: This is where the tank wins. Your kit is entirely physical, so once Maokai is into Bramble Vest and armor, your R crash-down and empowered autos bounce off and your burst just feeds his sustain. He's also the better teamfight tool — Twisted Advance and his ult zone or lock your carries while you can't melt him down. Convert your Level 6 window into a CS or plate lead, then sidelane and let your team play front-to-back; you do not out-scale a Maokai into items.
edits.after: This is where the tank wins. Your kit is entirely physical, so once Maokai is into armour your slam and empowered autos bounce off — and every spell you land shortens Sap Magic's heal, so the burst funds his sustain. Nature's Grasp rolls a rooting wall up the lane from 3000 range while Twisted Advance locks your carries. Convert your Level 6 window into a CS or plate lead, then sidelane and let your team play front-to-back; you do not out-scale a Maokai into items.

edits.before: His Sap Magic sustain and saplings heal off your cone-Q chip while your Q/E cooldowns are long — he sits even-to-ahead at level 1.
edits.after: Sap Magic heals him on attack and every spell you land shortens that cooldown, so your cone-Q chip pays for his sustain — even-to-ahead at 1.

edits.before: You get your Drakehound's Step weave online, but his Twisted Advance root and Q knockback still answer the trade — roughly even, don't force it.
edits.after: Your Drakehound's Step weave is online and he has no armour yet — but hold it until Twisted Advance's 14s is spent, or the root ends the trade.

edits.before: Your short Q-into-empowered-auto combo is up, but his sustain refills what you chip, so trades net neutral at best.
edits.after: Full pattern at 3 and he is still soft — trade after Bramble Smash, only 7s at rank 1, and leave before the root.

edits.before: Twisted Advance comes back faster than your full combo cycle here and he out-sustains your chip — he owns your weakest window.
edits.after: Twisted Advance at 14s beats your Lacerate 13s and Repudiation 18s cycle, and he out-sustains the chip — your weakest window.

edits.before: Public Execution blinks behind an immobile, dash-less Maokai and suppresses him — your one guaranteed all-in before he buys armor.
edits.after: Public Execution suppresses him on arrival, but it cannot target him mid-Twisted-Advance — fire it after the root, never into the dash.

edits.before: Even on your Eclipse/Profane Hydra spike, his armor and Sap Magic blunt your AD-only burst — the chunk just heals back.
edits.after: Eclipse and Profane Hydra land, but armour and Sap Magic blunt AD-only burst — Grievous Wounds is what makes the spike real.

edits.before: Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade. Only take the trade when Maokai's Twisted Advance is down.
edits.after: Repudiation is your shield, not the passive — and every spell you land on him shortens Sap Magic's heal.

edits.before: - Maokai Twisted Advance: matchup-defining — His lock-on root. Dash it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Maokai Twisted Advance: 14s at rank 1 — untargetable in transit, roots on arrival. Fire R after it, never into it. - Bramble Smash: 7s knockback. - Sapling Toss: 18s. - Nature's Grasp: 130s, 3000 range.

edits.before: His lock-on root. Dash it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 14s at rank 1, untargetable in transit. Engage once it is spent.

notes: Three things drove this rewrite: Maokai was described as immobile when Twisted Advance is a dash, Public Execution was again credited with armour penetration and healing it does not have, and Sap Magic's real rule was missing. That last one inverts the advice — Riot's text says his heal cooldown is reduced every time he casts a spell OR is struck by an enemy's spell, so chip poke accelerates his sustain and Grievous Wounds is the answer instead of more chip. Maokai's Bramble Smash carries derived 'grounding' and 'knockup' flags that Riot's own text (knockback and slow) does not support, and Sapling Toss carries a 'knockup' flag its text does not support either; I claimed neither.
